The core mechanism operates through iterative denoising followed by refinement of body poses to align with player locations. Initially, noisy body pose estimates are identified and corrected via normalization and filtering. Subsequent refinement applies machine learning models to enhance positional accuracy of limbs, torso, and head. This process is repeated until convergence, enabling accurate 2D-to-3D projection. Failure modes include overfitting to noise or underfitting due to insufficient resolution in ML models. The dual nature of this process—denoising and refinement—creates a feedback loop where each iteration improves the next. The system assumes that body pose data can be modeled as a noisy signal with a latent true structure. The breakdown regime occurs when noise overwhelms signal or when the correction algorithm cannot resolve fine-grained positional differences. This leads to misalignment between pose and actual player location, undermining downstream applications like 3D play area projection.
